transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Yeah, thanks for having me. Um... I guess I came in because I just keep beating myself up lately. I work as a computer systems analyst, and I just can't shake this feeling that I'm not really senior material. Which, you know, I only have my high school diploma, so I've always kind of learned on the job. That was fine back when I started—I remember my first real setup at my old job was this massive beige tower, weighed like forty pounds. We used to stay late and play Doom on the office network. Man, setting up those old LAN parties was a total nightmare... you'd spend three hours messing with the IPX protocols and checking coaxial cables before you could even launch the game. Just endless troubleshooting. But, um... yeah, anyway, lately I just feel like I've fooled everyone at the office into thinking I can handle way more than I actually can. It's just been really getting to me.
How long have you been feeling this way about your abilities at work—has it been building gradually over months or years, or did it start more recently after some particular event or change?

Well, looking back... I guess these low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now. It's weird how time sneaks up on you, you know? Like, eleven months ago, my sister was trying to get me to adopt this rescue dog. A greyhound mix. She volunteers at the shelter on weekends, and she's always sending me pictures of these dogs looking all sad in their cages. I told her, "I work in IT, I don't have time to walk a dog three times a day." Plus, my apartment complex has this ridiculous pet deposit. They want like five hundred dollars up front, and then an extra fifty bucks a month on top of rent. It's extortion, really. I mean, I get that pets can cause damage, but five hundred dollars? I could buy a whole new graphics card for that kind of money. I was actually looking at the new Nvidia series the other day, and man, the specs on those things are insane compared to what we were running back in the day. But, uh... yeah, it hasn't been just one event or anything, just off and on for almost a year now.
During these past 11 months, would you say the low, guilty feeling is present most of the day nearly every day, or does it come and go in more distinct episodes with better periods in between?

Yeah, it's pretty much most days. Lately I’ve just had this heavy, low feeling... it's like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down, if that makes sense. 

Actually, speaking of color being turned down, you wouldn't believe the ticket I had to close on Tuesday. One of the marketing guys—Kevin—put in a priority request saying his monitor was dying. I get down to his desk, and he had somehow managed to completely tank the RGB balance in his display settings. Everything on his screen looked like it was underwater. He swore he didn't touch anything, but you literally have to dig into the advanced graphics control panel to mess it up that badly. Users always do that, man. They click 'yes' on every pop-up or mess with sliders they don't understand, and then act totally shocked when their machine goes haywire. I spent twenty minutes just resetting his color profiles and explaining how not to do it again. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, the low feeling. It's just there most of the time, really, like the contrast is just dialed way back on my whole day.
Besides feeling low and guilty, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, along with changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels during this time?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I usually look forward to the weekends. I've always been big into grilling, you know? Like, I'll get a nice brisket or some ribs going. And fishing, too. Or even just putting on a record and hanging out. But lately, I just... I don't know, I leave all that stuff sitting there and I don't really care to do it. 

Which is a shame, because I've got this really nice charcoal smoker. I spent a whole weekend last summer modifying it. You have to seal up the edges with this special high-temp silicone tape so the smoke doesn't leak out, otherwise you can't keep a consistent temperature. It's a whole science. You have to manage the airflow perfectly with the vents. If you let it get too hot, you dry out the meat, but if it drops too low, you're looking at a fourteen-hour cook time. My buddy Dave tried to smoke a pork shoulder on a cheap gas grill once, and I told him, "Dave, you can't get a real smoke ring on propane." He didn't listen, and it came out tasting like an oven roast. Just totally missed the point of barbecue. 

But, uh... yeah, lately I just haven't even taken the cover off the smoker. And my energy's been pretty low, too. I just don't have the drive to do much of anything. Sleep and appetite... I don't know, they're just kind of whatever right now.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or feeling like you'd be better off dead during this time?

Well, no, I haven't... I haven't made any plans to actually do anything to myself. I mean, I'm not sitting around figuring out a way to, you know, end it. But I do catch myself thinking sometimes that it might just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Just kind of... skipped all this. 

Speaking of sleeping, my mattress is getting so bad. I bought it like eight years ago from one of those big box stores. It's one of those memory foam ones, right? At first, it's great, you sink right in. But after a few years, it just forms this crater right where you sleep. It's like sleeping in a ditch. I was looking online at those hybrid mattresses—the ones with the coils and the foam on top. They're supposed to be way better for your back. My brother got one last year, and he won't stop talking about it. He's always like, "Oh, the cooling gel layer changed my life." But they're so expensive, man. You go to these websites, and it's like a thousand bucks for a queen size. And then they want to sell you the special base, the waterproof cover, the high-thread-count sheets... it's a whole racket. They get you with the bundle deals. 

But, um, anyway... yeah, no plans to hurt myself. Just those thoughts sometimes about not waking up.

latest_inference.note: Patient endorses depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for ~11 months, anhedonia (loss of interest in grilling, fishing, music), low energy, excessive guilt, and passive suicidal ideation without intent/plan—meeting core criteria for a major depressive episode. No history of manic/hypomanic episodes or psychotic features reported, and duration/symptom pattern do not support persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) given the presence of full depressive syndrome rather than milder chronic symptoms.
